statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Company Registrar Online Portal (Samoa International Finance Authority eServices)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in Roman script; foreign-language names must be transliterated into English. Chinese or other script names may be included in the articles as a parallel trade name if a certified English translation is attached, but the certificate of incorporation will record only the English/Roman-script legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the registered agent may request a 30-day extension of the previous reservation if one remains. An administrative appeal must be lodged with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, accompanied by a legal submission from Samoan counsel. If the Registrar upholds the refusal, an appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour may be filed within 21 days, with final judicial review available in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted as the operational model, but the registered office must be a physical office maintained by a licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa. registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5% per year for a standard international company with no local physical presence; may increase to 25% if the entity or its UBO becomes subject to a sanctions/PEP trigger or if SIFA conducts a thematic inspection of the registered agent's files).

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or capital deposit rule. Subscribers may declare a nominal stated capital of USD 1 or such amount as set out in the Memorandum; shares may be unissued, partly paid, or fully paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Name Clearance Desk, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application specifying the proposed company name, intended ISIC 7110 virtual performance hosting scope, and proposed directors. The Registrar verifies that the name is not identical or deceptively similar to existing names and does not include prohibited expressions.
required_dossiers: Copy of the proposed name clause in the draft Memorandum
Certified passport copy of each subscriber and intended director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an alternate name or appeal by written submission within 7 days; no additional fee is charged for a replacement name lodged within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution, Notarization, and Attestation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths in Apia, Samoa; alternatively, a Samoa consular officer abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers and directors execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association before the notary. The notary verifies identity and proof of address, attests to the signatures, and certifies the notarized M&A set for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as director and secretary
Certified passport copy of each signatory
Proof of residential address dated within 3 months
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags a signature or attestation defect, re-execute the affected pages and obtain a fresh notarization before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form IC-1 together with the notarized M&A, a statutory declaration of compliance, and the registered office consent. Pay the USD 100 official fee by bank transfer, demand draft, or direct payment at SIFA's cashier. The Registrar reviews, enters the company on the international register, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory Declaration of Compliance under ICA 1987, s. 12
Registered office consent from the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or deficiency notice, correct the specified errors by supplementary affidavit and resubmit within 14 days; if registration is refused, an appeal lies to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registed Agent on the SIFA registered agent list, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent physically maintains the company's registered office address, displays the company name in accordance with ICA 1987, and submits or retains the registered agent acceptance form and registered office confirmation in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Company board resolution adopting the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent resigns or cannot act, appoint a successor agent within 30 days and file the notice of change with SIFA to avoid deregistration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company and its corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board issues share certificates, opens and maintains the statutory minute book and share register, and adopts operational resolutions for the virtual concert platform. The directors then complete KYB/CDD and activate payment rails, including Stripe or a USDC virtual account, in the company's name.
required_dossiers: Board resolution authorizing bank and payment processor accounts
KYB/KYC package of directors, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payments processor requests enhanced due diligence, furnish a corporate structure diagram, source of funds declaration, and any additional beneficial ownership particulars to the institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — no operating, manufacturing, or venue-building permit is required for the ISIC 7110 virtual concert metaverse service in Samoa.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) - national tax administration operating under the Ministry of Revenue; e-Services, TIN and VAGST registration portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws. Offshore International Company status and tax-exemption certification are administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA): https://www.sifa.ws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 through a SIFA-licensed registered agent. 2) The offshore IC is non-resident and, unless it carries on business in Samoa, has no statutory obligation to obtain a Samoan TIN or VAGST number; s.220 of the IC Act exempts it from all Samoan taxes on offshore operations. 3) If the IC engages in a Samoan taxable activity, elects voluntary VAGST registration, or needs a TIN for refund claims, the non-resident shareholder files Form TIN-01 with SRA (certified IC certificate, memorandum, passport copies, agent engagement letter, trade description) and, where taxable turnover reaches or is expected to exceed WST 80,000 in 12 months, files VAGST Form VAGST-01 with a Samoan address for service. 4) The Commissioner issues the TIN and VAGST registration number in approximately 14-30 working days; registration is effective from the date of application or commencement of taxable activity, whichever is earlier. 5) Pure offshore metaverse ticket income from non-resident buyers falls outside the Samoan registration nexus; a TIN application is nonetheless recommended where the IC banks in Samoa or seeks a binding SRA ruling.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - the Samoa International Company is statutorily classified as an offshore non-resident company wholly exempt from Samoan income tax, address tax, VAGST, and stamp duty on operations conducted outside Samoa (International Companies Act 1987, s.220; Income Tax Act 2016, s.4; VAGST Act 2003).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Samoa. The IC's exempt classification is fixed by statute and evidenced by a SIFA/SRA Tax Exemption Certificate. Available statutory elections: (i) voluntary VAGST registration under VAGST Act 2003, s.8, even below the WST 80,000 threshold; (ii) elective continuance/redomiciliation out of Samoa or conversion into a resident domestic company under the Companies Act 2006, which terminates the exemption; (iii) binding ruling applications to the Commissioner under the Tax Administration Act 2016 on whether a foreign-issued instrument is debt or equity; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act 2016 apply mandatorily to deny double non-taxation, with no elective carve-out for ICs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) - destination-based VAT under the VAGST Act 2003, as amended, administered by SRA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 80,000 (Samoan Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period, or expected next-12-months taxable turnover; all persons carrying on a taxable activity in Samoa crossing the threshold must register (VAGST Act 2003, s.8).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or mandatory digital stamping regime is in force in Samoa. Registered persons must issue sequentially numbered VAGST tax invoices with the statutory particulars (name, TIN, date, description, VAGST-exclusive amount, tax, total) under VAGST Act 2003, s.23, and retain records within Samoa for 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 2016. Digital ticketing transactions (Stripe receipts, USDC smart-contract logs) are accepted as commercial evidence; no SRA fiscal seal or e-invoice clearance is required for metaverse ticket sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the VAGST Act 2003, Second Schedule: (a) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply, evidenced by customs documentation; (b) services supplied to a non-resident person, or services supplied in relation to goods situated outside Samoa, provided the services are not performed on land or moveable property in Samoa and the place of effective use and enjoyment is outside Samoa; (c) digital supplies of virtual event admission and tokenized/NFT tickets to non-resident consumers, including metaverse-distributed tickets paid via Stripe or USDC, qualify as offshore services at 0% where the recipient is non-resident and the performance platform is outside Samoa. Input VAT attributable to such zero-rated supplies is refundable through the quarterly VAGST return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs) - only where physical goods or promotional merchandise are shipped; pure digital ticket supplies require no customs declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Samoan bank or authorized foreign-exchange dealer evidencing crediting or conversion of export proceeds
VAGST tax invoice and commercial invoice addressed to the non-resident purchaser
Platform performance records - Stripe settlement reports, USDC transfer hashes, and metaverse access logs demonstrating offshore delivery and foreign consumer location
SIFA International Company certificate and Tax Exemption Certificate
Signed service agreement or ticket-issuance terms designating the offshore venue of performance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SRA audit windows of 4 years (7 years where omission exceeds 25% of income; 10 years for fraud) allow retrospective rejection of export zero-rated treatment, clawback of refunds, and 2%-per-month late-payment interest under the Tax Administration Act 2016. Shortfall penalties escalate at 25% (voluntary disclosure), 75% (intentional disregard), and 150% (fraudulent evasion). Willful VAGST evasion is criminally punishable under VAGST Act 2003, s.45 by a fine up to WST 2,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years; false export declarations additionally attract Customs Act 2014 penalties, and exchange-control violations under Central Bank of Samoa regulations can suspend the IC's banking rails. A fraudulent zero-rating claim may also trigger SIFA revocation of the International Company's exempt status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Faletaoi, Apia, Samoa
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a regulated exchange-control regime under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and associated CBS directives. The Samoan Tālā (WST) is partially convertible for current-account transactions, with no major restrictions on trade-related payments, royalties, or service fees, provided supporting documentation is filed with authorized foreign-exchange dealers. Capital-account transactions and profit remittances by onshore resident entities require prior CBS approval and are subject to documentary review. However, a Samoa International Company (WS_IC) beneficially owned by non-residents and transacting solely in foreign currency is treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes. Such an entity may hold foreign-currency bank accounts and repatriate profits or dividends offshore without CBS conversion approval, provided that no WST-denominated transactions occur within the domestic economy. The virtual concert/metaverse ticketing activity (ISIC 7110) is an export of digital services, and therefore proceeds received in USD, USDC, or other convertible currencies are freely retained in offshore settlement accounts. Material hurdles to profit remittance are limited to standard tax-exempt status confirmation (International Companies Act 2012, Section 130), KYC/AML compliance, and the completion of CBS Form X-20 when a domestic WST account is used for incidental expenses. No capital-gains tax, withholding tax, or exchange-control surcharge is imposed on distributions to non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Exchange Control Act 1976 does not impose any fixed statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio on export proceeds earned by non-resident international companies. Resident exporters must surrender export proceeds to a licensed bank within 90 days of shipment, but WS_IC entities are exempt because they are classified as non-resident under the Exchange Control (International Companies) Exemption Notice 1988. For the virtual concert business, all proceeds from ticket sales, NFT/utility-token sales, and metaverse merchandise are treated as foreign-currency export receipts. The company may hold these receipts indefinitely in Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs) at commercial banks in Samoa or off-shore. If the IC voluntarily credits WST-denominated accounts, the exchange-control regime applies to the conversion, and the acquiring bank must obtain CBS approval for credits exceeding WST 500,000 per transaction. Recommended practice is to maintain 100% foreign-currency treasury positions with no conversion to WST, thereby eliminating surrender obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (WST only with prior CBS approval for FX conversion)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Samoa does not recognize offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) as licensed financial institutions. Only CBS-licensed commercial banks may provide payment and settlement services inside Samoa. The WS_IC may lawfully use foreign-based EMIs (e.g., Stripe, Airwallex) for receiving digital ticketing proceeds, but those EMIs do not hold a Samoan banking licence and cannot open a Samoan BIC/IBAN. Legal constraints: (1) the IC must not route payments through an EMI to a Samoan resident counterparty in violation of the Financial Institutions Act 2011; (2) crypto-fiat conversions executed by an EMI are permissible only if the EMI has valid anti-money-laundering controls under its home jurisdiction; (3) the Central Bank of Samoa does not provide a sandbox or passporting regime for foreign EMIs; (4) for settlement into the Samoan banking system, the IC must ultimately sweep funds to a CBS-licensed commercial bank. Recommended architecture: use Stripe (Asia-Pacific entity) for card acquiring, settle USD via SWIFT MT103 into a BSP Samoa FCA, and hold USDC in a non-custodial wallet or regulated custodian for metaverse disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permitted for international companies if the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and directors pass enhanced due diligence, but most Samoan banks require at least one director or a designated authorized signatory to attend an in-person identity verification interview at the bank's branch in Apia. This is a de facto KYC standard rather than a statutory requirement. For WS_IC entities with no physical office in Samoa, banks accept a remote video interview if the UBO has a relationship with a correspondent bank in an acceptable jurisdiction (e.g., Australia, New Zealand, Singapore). The bank may appoint a “trusted introducer” – typically a registered law firm, registered agent service provider, or an existing commercial bank client – to certify the identity of signatories. The International Company must verify the registered agent in Samoa (licensed under the International Companies Act 2012) and submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum & Articles, Certificate of Good Standing, and a board resolution authorizing the account opening. Practical assessment: Full remote opening is possible with BSP and ANZ for low-risk digital services entities, but due to the virtual concert and crypto exposure, lenders are expected to mandate a one-time physical or video interview with the UBO and the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director appears in politically exposed persons (PEP) databases or has residency in high-risk FATF grey-list countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide explainable source-of-wealth statements (asset declarations, tax returns from home jurisdiction), clean background check certificates from the UBO's national police, sworn affidavit of non-engagement in illegal concert ticketing schemes, and a legal opinion from a Samoan attorney confirming no conflict with CBS AML guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital asset/cryptocurrency exposure (USDC payments) triggers enhanced monitoring and possible adverse risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the exchange's Business Continuity Plan, audited proof that USDC is reserved 1:1 by Circle (USDC attestation report), a detailed transaction-flow diagram showing that only fiat-equivalent stablecoins are received and immediately converted to USD via a regulated exchange, and a policy signed by the CEO pledging to reimburse any fraud victim from ticket sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company has no physical office and only virtual/online sales, creating an underground conduit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide tax-exempt status certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Customs and Revenue, audited financial statements prepared by a CPA licensed in Samoa, executed contracts with concert artists indicating real commercial substance, and evidence of registration under the International Companies Act 2012 with licensed registered agent details.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction size or velocity for a small company (e.g., $5M+ monthly ticket sales) lacking transaction history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a complete chain of verified host ticketing logs (server metadata, blockchain minting timestamps), the platform's regulatory compliance attestation (SOC 2 Type II), a legal opinion from the Jersey or Singapore counsel confirming ticket resale caps, and a monthly treasury report with real-time liquidity forecasting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire transfers from sanctioned jurisdictions or use of crypto-mixers as payment rail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement geo-blocking of OFAC/UN/EU-sanctioned countries in the ticketing platform, confirm that USDC transfers are only accepted from whitelisted smart-contract addresses, and enhance the bank reference letters and stakes' certificate of incorporation. Also appoint an independent AML Monitor (e.g., Fintel Advisory) to conduct quarterly transactional screening and report to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the WS_IC may be made via SWIFT MT103 remittance from the shareholder's bank into the company's Foreign Currency Account at BSP Samoa (account currency USD). Compliant wiring must include the transaction purpose code '110 – Capital subscription' (in accordance with the CBS Exchange Control Form F) and must state in the remittance details: 'INVESTMENT IN INTERNATIONAL COMPANY – WS_IC – SHARE PLAN'. Beneficiary bank: Bank of South Pacific Samoa Limited, Apia, WS; SWIFT: BOSPSWSM; Beneficiary account name: [WS_IC Legal Name]; Address: Level 2, BSP Life Building, Apia. The bank will require the filing of a 'Certificate of Receipt of Foreign Currency' under CBS Notice 8/1988. Verification requirements: (a) Board resolution authorizing share issuance; (b) subscription agreement; (c) source-of-funds documents for the remitting shareholder (bank solvency certificate, six months of bank statements); (d) the IC's registered agent certification. For shareholders using cryptocurrency as the injection medium, the crypto must first be liquidated into USD through a CBS-licensed or well-known exchange and then wired via SWIFT; direct crypto-in-cash to the IC is not permitted by Samoan banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are governed by the Samoan Automated Clearing House (SACH) and SWIFT for cross-border transfers. For virtual concert artist royalties, mechanic fees, licensing fees, and metaverse infrastructure costs, the WS_IC may route outbound USD payments using: (1) SWIFT MT103 for traditional bank wires to artist agencies – maximum USD 2 million per transaction without pre-approval; (2) for recurring micro-entitlements to individual artists, use a commercial Letter of Credit (LC) if the recipient demands guaranteed payment, although LC usage is rare in digital services; (3) for disbursements to stablecoin addresses, the company may effect payment from its regulated crypto exchange account (e.g., Circle Business Account) via the Ethereum/Solana network, subject to the exchange's own KYC verification. Samoan exchange control (CBS Circular No. 12/2019) requires all outbound payments of USD 50,000 or more to be accompanied by an 'Outbound Transfer Form' (EBF-3) with the underlying contract or invoice attached. For USDC-denominated disbursements to vendors residing in non-FATF jurisdictions, the company must maintain a resolution from the bank confirming that the withdrawal from the FCA to a crypto exchange is permitted for trade settlements and that the exchange is not treated as a 'cash withdrawal'. The recommended clearing rail for large artist advances is a direct SWIFT MT103 from BSP Samoa; for ticket revenue payouts to settled legal entities, use MT103; for micro-royalties under USD 500, use cross-border automated clearing house (SEPA-CN or ACH) after conversion to EUR/USD via the EMI.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX Contracts (USD/EUR, USD/AUD) with licensed Samoan commercial banks, up to 12-month tenor, subject to CBS notification via Form FX-H4
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on THB / JPY / SGD through correspondent banks in Singapore (available via ANZ Samoa), provided the reference currency is not WST
Currency Swaps (USD/AUD/USD/EUR) with ANZ Bank Samoa or BSP Samoa for treasury risk management, permitted under CBS Financial Market Dealings Notice 2018
FX Options (plain vanilla) purchased from Bank of South Pacific Treasury Division, exercise 6-12 months, for hedging flow receipts from virtual ticket sales

Currency Swaps using USDC as a tokenised USD equivalent to hedge short-term stablecoin volatility (approved only if the bank recognises USDC as a non-deliverable underlying; customary risk agreement signed)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: International Companies in Samoa are generally exempt from the mandatory statutory audit requirement unless the company's articles of association expressly require an audit, or the Registrar or a regulatory authority imposes such a requirement for a specific licensed or public-interest activity. A company with more than 10 shareholders or with public fundraising may also become subject to audit as a condition of registration.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) if an audit is required; small and non-audited entities may maintain internal books using a recognized accounting basis consistent with the International Companies Act and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must obtain and retain current beneficial ownership information at incorporation, upon any share transfer, and at least annually thereafter. No public UBO register is filed with the Registry, but the agent is obligated to maintain a confidential UBO record and to report to Samoa's Financial Intelligence Unit upon request or suspicious activity. Annual confirmation is documented through a management declaration or director certificate, including confirmation of any change in ownership.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 4,500 per audit engagement, if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012; 0% for an International Company (IC) by virtue of section 212 of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), which creates a complete and permanent statutory exemption from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty in respect of the IC, its operations, and its property.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Total statutory exemption for International Companies: no corporate income tax, no branch profits tax, no capital gains tax, and no tax on distributions. The only mandatory state payments are the annual Government fee and the annual Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) fee, both calculated on authorised share capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form 3 under the International Companies (Fees and Forms) Regulations); electronically lodged by the licensed Samoan registered agent through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual fee payable on the anniversary date of incorporation; the annual return must be filed within three months after that anniversary date (a fixed 30 June filing cycle may be adopted by election).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name, registration number, date of incorporation, and anniversary date of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name appearing on the Certificate of Incorporation; do not use trade names or metaverse platform aliases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B - Registered Office and Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and the name and licence number of the Samoan registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office must be the agent's physical Samoan address, not a post office box; a virtual concert operator must not substitute a foreign or virtual address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents and has not held property situated in Samoa unless duly licensed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A metaverse ticketing issuer must verify that no Samoan-resident support services, local distribution, or Samoan-situs digital assets are being provided to or held by the IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, and nationalities of all directors and shareholders, and the physical location of the register of members.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate directors, disclose the ultimate beneficial ownership chain to the registered agent for AML record-keeping requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part E - Authorised Capital and Fee
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised share capital, number of issued shares, and the computed Government and SIFA annual fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee tiers are triggered by authorised capital; confirm the maximum authorised capital before filing to avoid overpayment or underpayment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed late penalty of SAT$500 plus a 10% per-annum surcharge on the unpaid annual fee; continued default leads to administrative strike-off from the Register after formal notice, restoration fees of up to SAT$1,000, and loss of the statutory tax exemption during any period of strike-off.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends paid by a Samoan resident company under the Income Tax Act 2012; 0% for dividends declared by an International Company, because the section 212 exemption applies both to the IC and to its distributions, making profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders entirely free of Samoan withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required for IC dividends because no Samoan source tax arises. Where a resident company would otherwise rely on treaty relief, the protocol is: obtain a Certificate of Residence from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, submit the TRC together with the prescribed relief declaration to the withholding agent before payment, and apply the applicable DTA rate at source. Samoa's only comprehensive double tax agreements in force are with Australia and New Zealand.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest 15%, royalties 15%; IC payers and payees enjoy a 0% source rate under the section 212 exemption. Treaty rates for Samoan resident companies under the Samoa-New Zealand DTA and the Samoa-Australia DTA cap source-based taxation on interest at 10% in ordinary financial arrangements, while dividends and royalties generally remain at the 15% domestic ceiling. Cross-border licensing of digital concert content or token-related IP to a Samoan IC is outside the Samoan taxing net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: None - Samoa has not enacted Local File or Master File documentation thresholds; the Income Tax Act 2012 contains only a general arm's length norm and general anti-avoidance provisions, which are inapplicable to a tax-exempt International Company, and no Samoan transfer pricing return is prescribed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Act 2021 requires an International Company carrying on a 'relevant activity' - including headquarters, distribution and service centre, pure equity holding, IP holding, financing and leasing, shipping, banking, insurance, or fund management - to demonstrate economic substance in Samoa: (i) board meetings and strategic direction exercised in Samoa; (ii) Samoan-resident employees proportionate to the core income-generating activities; (iii) adequate operating expenditure incurred in Samoa; and (iv) an annual economic substance notification filed with SIFA. A metaverse IP-holding or service-coordinating IC must satisfy this test in Samoa, not merely in the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly lodging false annual returns, concealing related-party service fees, or misrepresenting the IC's relationship with Samoan residents to preserve the statutory exemption (Tax Administration Act 2012).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded plus statutory late-payment interest; criminal conviction for individuals: fine up to SAT$50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years; for companies: fine up to SAT$100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorise false statements face personal criminal prosecution, civil restitution orders for the full tax shortfall, departure prohibition orders, disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a pure shell with no Samoan physical presence, no local board meetings, and no substance documentation while claiming the section 212 exemption, or carrying on business with Samoan residents without a licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty not exceeding SAT$50,000 under the Economic Substance Act 2021; administrative strike-off and deregistration for non-payment of fees; upon deregistration, the IC's contracts, including digital ticket tokenisation and concert hosting agreements, may become unenforceable, and the tax exemption may be retrospectively withdrawn for the default period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil: directors and controlling shareholders become jointly and severally liable for debts contracted during the shell period, face director disqualification orders, and may be barred from re-entry to Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the virtual concert platform, NFT ticket tokens, Stripe payment rails, or USDC transfers to receive, convert, or transfer criminal proceeds, or failing to disclose beneficial ownership to the registered agent (Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On indictment: imprisonment up to 14 years and/or a fine up to SAT$1,000,000; on summary conviction: imprisonment up to 3 years and/or a fine up to SAT$200,000; tainted assets, including virtual assets and cryptocurrency, are subject to confiscation orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge or reckless disregard face personal criminal liability, asset freezing and restraint orders, international extradition exposure, and travel bans; AML statutory fines are not dischargeable through corporate winding-up.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to operate the metaverse ticketing platform or processing Stripe and USDC payouts after the IC has been administratively struck off the Register for non-filing of the annual return or non-payment of annual fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offence under the International Companies Act: fine up to SAT$50,000 plus a daily continuing default penalty of SAT$500; all contracts entered into while struck off, including ticket sales, hosting agreements, and token smart contracts, are unenforceable against the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who participates in post-strike-off trading is personally liable without limitation for the company's debts and obligations arising in that period and may be subject to disqualification orders and civil recovery proceedings.
